LanguageData.NHCP.TabSubLabel_FuelDescription: Enabled things can be used as fuel.
LanguageData.NHCP.TabSubLabel_CommonalityDescription:
Commonality is a WEIGHT, not a percentage - the game compares a material's value against every other material's before picking one, so what matters is the value relative to everything else, not the number by itself.
Vanilla reference points: Gold 0.02, Plasteel 0.05, Leather 0.10-0.24, Wood and Steel 1.0, Cloth 1.4.
0 means never picked by any weighted choice - safe to use as a hard "off" switch. 100 (roughly 100x Wood) means picked almost every time, but never truly guaranteed - it still has to beat whatever else is competing, and the share it gets shrinks as more materials are available.
A few generators (e.g. some default-stuff fallbacks) pick without weighting commonality at all, so even a material set to 0 can occasionally still turn up there.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_Logging: Logs some information, mostly on game start.\nYou probably don't want it on.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_MergeCategory: [EXPERIMENTAL] Creates a {0} category and gathers New Harvest {1} into it, along with matching items from other mods, attempting to replace their original "{1}" categories.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_ResourceReadout: Shows the {0} category as a primary resource on the resource readout.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_MoveDrinksToVBECatego: Move Medicinal Drinks Into Vanilla Brewing Expanded Category
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_MoveDrinksToVBECate: Move New Harvest medicinal drinks to Vanilla Brewing Expanded's non-alcoholic category.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_AddAquaticReedsToBiom: Add New Harvest Reeds To Biomes
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddAquaticReedsToBi: Adds aquatic New Harvest reeds to biomes containing Odyssey reeds at 25% their frequency.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddMoreWoodFloors: Add more floors using New Harvest wood.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_NewHarvestNonWoodFloo: New Harvest Non-Wood Floors To Dropdown
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_NewHarvestNonWoodFl: Group New Harvest non-wood floors in a single dropdown.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_NewHarvestWoodFloorsT: New Harvest Wood Floors To Dropdowns
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_NewHarvestWoodFloor: Group New Harvest wood floors into dropdowns.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_BaseWoodFloorsToDro: Group base wood floors in a dropdown.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_ModWoodFloorsToDrop: Group mod-added wood floors in dropdowns.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddWoodDryads: Add new dryad types to make cedar, ebony, mahogany or rosewood logs.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddHayConversionRec: Adds a Crafting Spot recipe to convert 50 New Harvest hay into base game hay.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddWoodConversionRe: Adds a Crafting Spot recipe to convert 50 New Harvest wood into base game wood.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_UseVanillaLogGraphi: Makes New Harvest Logs use colored vanilla log textures.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_Commonality: The value written directly onto this material. Every weighted pick in the game reads it - buildings, weapons, apparel, trader stock, quests. 0 turns this material off everywhere; nothing will pick it.\nRight-click to reset to this material's default.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_BaseCommonality: The reference point the three settings below scale from. Alone controls everything they do NOT reach: trader stock, quest and reward generation, and Vanilla Expanded Framework's own structure generator.\n0 turns this material off everywhere, including the three settings below - they have nothing to scale.\nRight-click to reset to this material's default.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_StructureCommonality: How often this material is chosen for generated buildings and furniture - except Vanilla Expanded Framework's own structure generator, which uses Base instead.\nRight-click to reset to this material's default.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_WeaponCommonality: How often this material is chosen for weapons carried by generated pawns. Weapons in trader stock or quest rewards use Base instead.\nRight-click to reset to this material's default.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_ApparelCommonality: How often this material is chosen for apparel worn by generated pawns. Apparel in trader stock or quest rewards uses Base instead.\nRight-click to reset to this material's default.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_CommonalityDisabledBy: Disabled because Base is 0. Raise Base above 0 to use this setting; the value kept here comes back with it.
LanguageData.NHCP.SectionLabel_FallColorTreesSectionS: Choose trees that will display fall colors.
LanguageData.NHCP.SectionLabel_MaterialColorsSectionS: Choose RGB (0-255) color values for materials.\nKeep in mind that most things are drawn with no tint in mind (255,255,255 (white)).\nThing is the actual item, like a wood log. Stuff is made out of the item, like a wall.
LanguageData.NHCP.Button_CategoryResetInfo: Things that originate in this category will moved back to it, and things that do not will be moved back to their respective categories, if applicable.
LanguageData.NHCP.Tooltip_EditCategoryContents: Choose which things belong to the {0} category.\nOnly available while merging is enabled for the category.
LanguageData.NHCP.EditCategory_RightClickHint: Right click to reset this entry.\nShift + right click to reset all entries.
LanguageData.NHCP.EditCategory_MoveHint: Right click to remove from {0} and add here.
LanguageData.NHCP.EditCategory_SearchTypes: Search by defName, label or category.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_HayNeedsCooling: If disabled, removes the need to refrigerate New Harvest hay.\nIt will instead just deteriorate if outdoors.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_GrainsProduceVCEFlour: Grains Produce Vanilla Cooking Expanded Flour
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_GrainsProduceVCEFlo: New Harvest grain plants will produce Vanilla Cooking Expanded flour as a secondary output, at the percentage of their grain yield set below.\n(Example: Amaranth plants will produce {0} amaranth grain and {1} flour)

New Harvest grain plants will be harvested for Vanilla Cooking Expanded flour instead of grain, at the percentage of their normal grain yield set below.\n(Example: Amaranth plants will produce {0} flour and no grain)
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderLabel_GrainFlourOutputPercent: Flour Output (% Of Normal Grain Yield)
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_GrainFlourOutputPerce:
How much flour a grain plant produces, as a percentage of the grain it would normally yield.

100% = one flour per grain.
50% = half as much flour as grain.
200% = twice as much flour as grain.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_GrainsProduceVCEFlo:
Grain plants are harvested for flour only - no grain is produced at all.
The percentage above still applies, measured against the plant's normal grain yield.
(Example: Amaranth plants will produce {0} flour and no grain)

Warning: the grain items themselves become unobtainable from farming. Any recipe that consumes them loses its renewable source.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddTruffleDiggingBe: Allows tamed pigs and dogs to dig up truffles when on diggable natural terrain.
LanguageData.NHCP.AdjusterTooltip_TicksBetweenTruffle: Ticks that must pass before an animal attempts to dig for truffles.\n2500 ticks = 1 game hour; 60000 ticks = 1 game day.
LanguageData.NHCP.RangeTooltip_TruffleDiggingChanceRa: Chance to successfully spawn a truffle on each dig attempt.\nThe maximum value is used first, then reduced by 'Chance Reduction Per Animal'.\nThe final chance will not fall below the minimum.
LanguageData.NHCP.SliderTooltip_TruffleDiggingChanceR: Amount the success chance is reduced for each animal capable of digging truffles.
LanguageData.NHCP.RangeTooltip_TruffleAmountRange: Range of truffles spawned when a dig attempt succeeds.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_TruffleSpawnsForbid: If enabled, truffles found by animals will spawn forbidden.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_TruffleGizmoRequire: If enabled, animals must be trained in Obedience, Dig, or Forage to receive the truffle digging command toggle. Otherwise, all tamed animals will always have the toggle.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxLabel_TreatFungusPoisoningL: Treat Mushroom Poisoning Like Food Poisoning
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_TreatFungusPoisonin: If enabled, pawns with genes, hediffs, or traits that reduce food poisoning chance also reduce the chance of new poison effects from New Harvest mushrooms that have poison effects.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddNourishedHediffF: If enabled, animals that eat New Harvest's Fodder Mix or Protein Kibble will become nourished causing them to nuzzle more often for a period of time.\nThe animal must be capable of nuzzling.
LanguageData.NHCP.AdjusterTooltip_NourishedHediffSeve: The average amount of game hours between nuzzle attempts while nourished.\nA smaller number means more attempts.
LanguageData.NHCP.RangeTooltip_NourishedHediffDuratio: The amount of ticks that the animal remains nourished.\nA random number within this range will be chosen when the animal becomes nourished.\n2500 ticks = 1 game hour; 60000 ticks = 1 game day.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_ChangeAnimalFoodRec: If enabled, New Harvest's Fodder Mix and Protein Kibble recipes can be crafted using a wider range of ingredients.
LanguageData.NHCP.CheckboxTooltip_AddMapleSyrupChain: If enabled, New Harvest's Sugar Maple trees will produce Maple Sap which must be boiled into Maple Syrup, instead of Maple Syrup coming directly from the trees.\nMaple Sap can be boiled wherever meals can be cooked.
LanguageData.NHCP.General_RightClickToReset: You can right click on tabs or settings to reset them.
